text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves almost nothing. Risk functions often have female-majority HR, compliance and regulatory staff, so a four-woman panel can arise by chance or org structure. Leading with it makes you look like you're building a narrative rather than a case, and it's the easiest point for them to dismiss.

The stronger ground is substantive: a head of risk modelling role can legitimately favour regulatory credibility over technical depth — supervisors are the main audience. So the credentials gap isn't damning either.

What is genuinely poor practice is the unanswered request. Chase it in writing, ask for the scoring criteria, weightings and your scores. If the criteria look retrofitted to her profile, that's when you have something.
